finding: The Federal Reserve's own FedNow live-participants workbook (fednow-live-participants.xlsx, list dated 11/02/26, parsed in-browser) lists 'CITIBANK, N.A.'. Every FedNow participant must at least receive credit transfers (participants are 'receive-only' or 'send and receive'; there is no send-only tier). Banking Dive (Mar 26 2026) confirms Citi joined FedNow in 2025.

claim: Send P2P from Citibank Debit Card via participating apps: $1,000/day, $10,000/month
finding: The chapter's own rail_participation.push_to_card and recent_changes state the Sept 19, 2026 CDAA amendment raised the debit-card P2P send limit from $1,000 to $2,500/day; the sub-product still carries the 2017 $1,000 figure. Reviewer's in-browser parse of CDAA.pdf (pages footed CMDPAGE0_261027) shows an amendment page deleting the 'Person to Person Payments / credit' rows of the base limits table (base table: Send $1,000/day); new values in that amendment are rendered in an embedded font the reviewer could not decode.

claim: Product name 'Debit card transfers (Mastercard MoneySend / Mastercard Send)'; statement labels 'MoneySend Credit'/'MoneySend Debit'
finding: 'MoneySend' and the statement labels come only from a January 2017 statement insert (S017). The current CDAA (Nov 20, 2025 + amendments) contains no 'MoneySend' or Mastercard reference for card P2P; it describes 'Person to Person Payments / credit' on the Citibank Banking Card and 'P2P payment transfers sent to a Citibank debit card'. The CitiBusiness manual uses 'DEBIT CARD TRANSFER CREDIT/DEBIT'. Mastercard Send as the rail is a reasonable inference (Banking Card is Mastercard-branded) but is not current bank wording.
resolution: Name 'Debit card person-to-person payments (Citibank Banking Card)'; network 'Mastercard Send (INFERRED)'; former name 'Mastercard MoneySend'; statement labels annotated as 2017 wording

claim: S031 'Citi Alliance Consumer Deposit Account Agreement' is cited as CONFIRMED_BANK evidence for mainstream Citibank consumer IIT, internal transfer, Global Transfer, bill-pay and Reg E claims
finding: CDAA_CA.pdf is the Citi Alliance agreement (effective Feb 13, 2024) for clients of external wealth firms; the current CDAA's Appendix 3 lists 'Citi Alliance® March 4, 2024' as a discontinued product. It is not the governing agreement for mainstream consumers. The reviewer re-found the key IIT text (9:30 PM ET cancel deadline; cancelling one cancels the series; 'no fees') in the current CDAA, so the facts largely stand, but the citation is wrong.
resolution: Cite S911 as primary; S031 kept as corroboration and annotated as a discontinued-program agreement

claim: Consumer bill pay: 'new individual payees become active after two business days (CBOL rule)'
finding: The two-business-day activation rule is taken from the CitiBusiness Online FAQ (S010), a business channel. Neither the consumer Online Bill Payment page nor the consumer Bill Pay Quick Start Guide (S002, which is the consumer 'Citibank Online' guide despite its CBOL_ filename) states it. Applying a business rule to a consumer journey is a misattribution.
resolution: Step marked INFERRED with the 'not published for consumers' wording

claim: 'Consumer external-account linking (IIT) documentation is thin: verification method, delivery speed and limits are not public'
finding: The live IIT page publishes timing (same-day ACH before 12:30 PM ET, next-day after) and tenured/untenured inbound/outbound daily and monthly limits; the chapter's own strengths already say so. Only the verification method remains undisclosed.
resolution: Weakness narrowed to the undisclosed verification method and the series-cancel rule

claim: 'Citibank Global Transfer Service: free, immediate Citi-to-Citi transfers domestically and cross-border, a rail no other top-4 US bank offers on-us'
finding: Live product page: 'no transfer fee' for international, but foreign-currency transfers carry an FX commission in the rate; funds move 'Once your transfer is reviewed' (no 'immediate' claim on the page); first-time transfers have lower limits. The 'no other top-4 US bank' comparison is not sourced.
resolution: Merged wording per challenge; peer comparison deferred to cross-bank synthesis

claim: Remote Check Deposit and Lockbox tagged rail CASH_ATM_BRANCH
finding: Schema vocabulary: CASH_ATM_BRANCH covers cash/ATM/branch deposits. RCD is scanner/mobile remote image deposit and Lockbox is a P.O.-box receivables service; neither is ATM/branch.
resolution: P13-S02 and S03 rail OTHER; P13 rails ['RTP','OTHER']

claim: Commercial/institutional coverage omits Citi Token Services
finding: Citi Token Services (tokenized deposits on a permissioned blockchain for 24/7 institutional liquidity and cross-border payments) is live in the United States and six other markets (press release Sept 28, 2026).

claim: Omits WorldLink Payment Services and the Sept 29, 2026 launch of multi-market instant payments on the Swift payments scheme
finding: Citi press release (Sept 29, 2026): first bank live with multiple markets on the Swift payments scheme via Global Clearing and WorldLink (AUD/NPP, GBP/FPS, INR/IMPS, and USD via expanded USD Clearing so participating banks can send dollar payments credited to Citi U.S. account holders in real time). Institutional only.
resolution: Add CITI-P14-S06 and a recent-change line

claim: No dated entry for the November 2026 Online Funds Transfer T&C update adding third-party AI-agent responsibility
finding: The live wire T&Cs flag 'November 2026 updates' that make the customer solely responsible for instructions given by any third-party AI agent. The chapter lists this only as a differentiator without a date.

Internal inconsistency on the 9.100.0 date. Reviewer's App Store fetch shows 9.100.0 as released within the last hour (i.e., Nov 6, 2026) with prior 9.99.0 dated Sep 24; Google Play shows an Oct 28 update. Apple date may reflect a phased/re-release.
resolution: Harmonised wording: 'iOS 9.100.0 (listing dated early Nov 2026; Google Play updated Oct 28, 2026)'; open question added. A dated Apple version-history screenshot would settle it.

claim: Zelle send authenticated with 'Face ID / Touch ID / 6 Digit PIN' (S016, S018)
finding: The '6 Digit PIN' language is in the Online Funds Transfer (wire) terms and concerns sign-on to set up a funds transfer; the App Store listing mentions Touch ID/Face ID sign-on but not a 6-digit PIN, and no Zelle source states a Zelle-specific step-up.
resolution: Step kept; evidence INFERRED; wording per challenge

claim: Wire 'cutoff 6:45 PM ET for same-business-day processing' sourced to S016
finding: The wire T&Cs say cut-off hour is 'disclosed ... at the time I request'; the 6:45 PM figure is on the live wire product page, which also gives 6:00 PM ET for international.
resolution: Source S917 added; supplementary cutoffs updated

claim: value is a free-text sentence rather than true/false/'unknown'
finding: Schema expects a boolean or 'unknown'. Evidence supports true (consumer/SMB receive and send via Citibank debit card in third-party apps; institutional send via Citi Payment Exchange).

claim: 'debit-card transfers are passive Mastercard Send acceptance with 2017-era limits [S017]'
finding: Same evidence as CITI-C002: the Sept 19, 2026 amendment raised the send limit, so '2017-era limits' no longer holds.
Citi's page says 'Recurring payments for ongoing bills'; 'standing orders' is not Citi US terminology.

claim: Bill pay feature set omits 'Bill payment check images as proof of payment'
finding: The live Online Bill Payment page lists check images as a feature.

claim: 'Citi joined FedNow in 2025 ... participation type not confirmed'
finding: Participation type is partly settled: listed by the Federal Reserve as a live participant, so at minimum receive (see CITI-C001). Send capability remains unconfirmed.
